anti_generic_signature_read: What stops it being generic is entirely the sphere art: the recognisable continental outline on the blue-green globe, the red oval on the banded giant, the steeply tilted band on the cyan one, the small dark oval on the blue one, and the tilted ring -- those are specific, and the size hierarchy is doing real work as a ranking system. On the red sphere, one dark region was singled out unprompted as the single shape worth naming: a shield or blunt arrowhead, flat across the top-left, tapering to a rounded point at the bottom.
blind_action_read: Three states of the same board, side by side. The first has the full complement of sixteen pieces, eight on white bases and eight on black, arrayed around the outer cells; the second has about eleven left and they have moved inward; the third has six. The terrain is identical across all three -- the same tiles in the same cells. Only the spheres move and disappear. A game in progress, pieces being removed.
blind_form_read: A flat rectangular slab board of 7x9 cells with narrow raised ribs, carrying square terrain plates at three heights -- brown plates with a shallow circular bowl ringed by small spikes, and orange and cyan plates recessed below the face. Each playing piece is a squat cylindrical disc base plus a sphere, the sphere diameter varying from about 0.35 to 0.75 of the base diameter across pieces. One sphere carries a flat annular ring about 1.6x its diameter, tilted off horizontal. Two flat trays each carry eight shallow circular recesses in a 4x2 array.
blind_held_read: A tabletop board game: a thick grey grid board with sculpted terrain inlays, sixteen marble-on-a-disc playing pieces, and two moulded storage trays.
blind_relationship_read: Two mirror sets of eight, distinguished only by base colour, each set containing one of each sphere type. They start along opposite outer rows facing each other with all the terrain in the contested middle. The two trays have exactly eight recesses each -- one slot per piece, one tray per side. The sphere size hierarchy reads as a rank hierarchy. Two opposing armies, a terrain-filled middle, and a per-side holding tray.
blind_subjects_read: The planets of the solar system, read off what is painted on them rather than from convention: one sphere unmistakably Earth, with green landmasses on blue ocean and a recognisable continental outline; one large sphere with horizontal tan-and-brown bands and a deep red oval spot; one pale yellow sphere with a tilted flat ring; one blue sphere with thin white latitude bands and a small grey-blue oval; one cyan sphere with a single broad band running as a steeply tilted great circle; one red sphere with a white polar cap and ochre patches; one plain pale grey. The terrain plates carry an engraved half-disc with radiating rays -- a rising sun.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Unprompted, before knowing circles were what this revision replaced: 'They are all faceted irregular polygons with straight edges and hard corners' -- listed individually as a shield/keystone, a rough hexagon, a chain of lozenges, a broad diagonal stripe, a rounded trapezoid. The word circle was never used of any albedo region. On re-measurement: no circular arcs and none of the lens-shaped scalloped notches a union of circles leaves at its intersections; in one view a single connected component carries 88% of the albedo pixels.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Mars's dark albedo is drawn as outline regions with irregular, connected outlines, not as a union of six circles.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Of all eight close-up views the reader singled out exactly one marking: 'a shield or keystone -- flat across the top-left, tapering to a rounded point at the bottom, with a notch bitten out of its lower-left. This is the one marking I would put a name to.' Re-cropped at 4x it is a downward-pointing triangle, and is the only isolated compact well-defined region on the globe -- everything else is an elongated band or a limb sliver. The reader did not identify it as Syrtis Major by name and said so.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: One dark wedge stands out from the rest -- Syrtis Major drawn as a dark triangle rather than a circle.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'A chain of three or four joined lozenges running horizontally right across the body -- a belt or band rather than a shape', read as a band without being told to look for one. Measured: one connected component of 16,984 px, 88% of that view's albedo, running from the left limb diagonally down to the right, pinching to a narrow waist mid-way but never breaking, sitting below the sphere's centre with the cap above it.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: A dark belt runs along the southern mid-latitudes, reading as one band rather than as separate spots.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Answering a question that did not mention circles: 'Irregular and angular -- not smooth and not circular. Looking straight down at the cap, its outline is roughly eight to ten straight segments forming a lumpy pentagon, with two deep concave notches biting into its lower-left... the cap's lower boundary is a stepped, spiky line -- it reads like torn paper, not like a drawn circle or an ellipse.' Measured on the two top-down views, rim radius swings sd/mean = 0.113 and 0.122 against the 0.00-0.01 a circle of latitude would give.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Both polar cap rims are broken so the edge is ragged, not an exact circle of latitude.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'The top-down views confirm the white cap is centred on the axis of rotation.' Cap area is 22,911 px against 22,821 px between the two pieces, a 0.4% difference. The reader later corrected their own wording: the cap centroid is offset from the sphere's projected centre by 0.29 and 0.17 of the radius, which is the cap sitting on a leaning pole rather than the cap being off-centre.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The caps are still centred on the poles, still caps, and were not made bigger or reshaped.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: A pixel census over every Mars view, classifying by chromaticity family with an explicit catch-all bucket: 'Other = 0.00% in all six single-piece images.' The brown is a single material, not two: G/R = 0.675 +/- 0.003 and B/R = 0.213 +/- 0.003 across all six, one albedo colour under varying illumination.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Mars carries exactly three filaments: a red globe, cocoa_brown albedo and white caps -- no fourth colour and no bright beige highlands.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: A test run blind, before the rule was known: 'I cropped both spheres, scaled them to a common size, mirrored one, and compared. Un-mirrored, the shield/keystone patch reads the same way on both spheres. Mirrored, it flips and no longer matches. So they are not mirror images.' On the reveal the reader measured the lean separately: the cap centroid's horizontal offset is opposite in sign between the two armies in all four paired views, magnitude about 0.37 of the radius, a lower bound of 21.7 degrees against Mars's true 25.19.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The two Mars pieces carry the same map, not a reflected one; what is mirrored between them is the lean.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'No circular pits, rims or bowls anywhere on either globe in any of the eight Mars views.' The reader noted that crater-like forms do exist elsewhere in the set -- blind they had described the asteroid-belt tiles as 'a large shallow circular bowl in the middle and a fringe of small tetrahedral spikes' -- and that those are board tiles, not Mars.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE -- no craters anywhere on Mars.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'No cone, no circular caldera, no radial flank pattern, and nothing breaking the globe's silhouette.' On the canyon, unprompted in the blind phase: 'no long horizontal gash'. The nearest thing is the southern belt, which is a broad lobed band, not a linear incision.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE -- no Olympus Mons or any volcano, and no Valles Marineris or any canyon.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Unprompted in the blind phase: 'no large dark circular basin'. On the reveal: no bright circular region exists; the only near-circular bright feature is the polar cap, and it is at the pole and jagged.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE -- no Hellas or any large bright basin.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'The albedo and cap are perfectly flush -- the globe's silhouette is a clean circle everywhere the markings reach it, and no marking casts an edge.' The one protrusion the reader found is the mounting seat collar at the globe's foot, which they measured as appearing identically in its own colour on every one of the sixteen worlds and identified as the set's common mounting seat rather than anything this revision introduced.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE -- nothing protrudes from the globe; every marking is flush and the outer surface stays an unbroken sphere.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Measured directly by dilating the cap mask and counting what the cap borders against: 'The fraction of cap-border pixels that are brown is 0.000 in all six views -- the cap sits directly on red for its entire perimeter.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE -- no dark collar or ring around either polar cap.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: 'The terrain is byte-for-byte identical across all three panels -- the same tiles in the same cells with the same cones', and the other fourteen worlds share the same shading language and the same mounting collar as Mars with nothing looking newly touched. The reader's independent count from the images -- 12 asteroid-belt tiles, 6 sunken corona cells, a 7x9 field -- matches the specification exactly.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NEGATIVE -- nothing else in the set changed; the board, belt, stars, corona cells, trays and the other fourteen worlds are ordinary members of the set.

largest_risk: Two things the images cannot settle, both disclosed rather than claimed. First, the north cap is required to be the larger and more irregular of the two, and no render in this set shows the south cap at all: the globe is sunk 2.00 mm into its disc and cut at the disc's top face, and at 25.19 degrees of obliquity that cut removes almost the whole southern cap. measure/mars-surface.md finds white at latitude -70 and nothing below it; measure/mars-atlas-resolution.md measures the asymmetry in the rings themselves -- six northern lobes reaching 0.77 mm past their rim against four southern reaching 0.51 -- but it is not visible on the finished piece and is not claimed to be. The critic recorded this requirement as not determinable and was right to. Second, every visual judgement in this run was made on images from cad/scripts/render_review, which applies a linear-to-sRGB encode to channels that colors.py seals as sRGB, so those images show cocoa_brown as #C5852A rather than #8E3C06 and put the albedo LIGHTER than the globe. On the sealed channels the shop reads, the albedo is the darker of the two, but only by a 1.88:1 contrast ratio -- under the 3:1 at which a value difference reads as lightness rather than hue. measure/filament-value.md measures both. Mars is required to keep exactly red, cocoa_brown and white, so the thin margin is stated and not fixed.
resolution: The blind read confirmed every positive and negative held-form requirement the images can carry, and no repair round was needed. The critic's three structural findings -- a cone passing through a sphere, Saturn's ring passing through its own base, and a disc straddling two terrain levels -- were each answered with a boolean rather than an argument: measure/seated-piece-clearance.md places all eight worlds at both seats the assembly gives them, beside the exact star and corona solids, and measures 0.000000 mm3 shared in all sixteen cases; inspect interfere reports clashCount 0 across the whole 182-occurrence assembly and inspect validate reports it sound. Those readings were coincident shared surfaces and projected overlap in a flat-shaded render with no ground plane or shadows, and on the reveal the critic withdrew three of their eleven findings as render artifacts and downgraded four more as by-design. The finding that stands is presentational and is recorded in antisol_spec.md section 11 item 17: the review renderer double-encodes colour, which is why an unprimed reader looked straight at Syrtis Major, called it the single most distinctive shape on the piece, and still read the markings as highlands rather than as dark albedo.
reviewer: independent native critic, given only the ten canonical images under neutral filenames and no Wish, concept or product name; the Wish was revealed only after the unprimed read was recorded
